purpose: Deepen the existing RISK_BEARING_ORCHESTRATOR and ACCESS_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSE mechanisms without creating a new ontology. Test whether latent value repeatedly begins to flow when ownership, performance, maintenance, residual-value, market or fulfillment risk is reassigned to the actor structurally better able to control it, and whether such reassignment requires trusted state/outcome verification.

evidence: XCMG's current joint-leasing structure has the lessor purchase the equipment, lease it to the user and use a professional operations/maintenance party for servicing.
At lease end the user can renew, return or purchase the asset.
XCMG explicitly describes this structure as suitable for short-term, temporary or seasonal needs, with lower cost, no user-side repair/maintenance burden and reduced technology-obsolescence risk.
findings.interpretation: The receiving actor buys temporary use-value instead of taking the full ownership, maintenance, residual-value and obsolescence bundle. This is a risk-allocation refinement of ACCESS_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSE, not a new equipment-rental opportunity.

evidence: Wuxi reported nearly 1,500 assistive-device lending/rental service uses and eight smart rental points before the 2026 expansion.

By 2026 Wuxi had arranged 50 community assistive-device rental points and a 57-product rental catalogue spanning wheelchairs, care beds, oxygen concentrators, rehabilitation devices and other categories.

The 2026 product-entry rules require repeat clean/disinfection durability, supplier maintenance training, local after-sales presence and warranty support; eligible users can rent for two- or three-month periods rather than purchase the asset.
findings.interpretation: Short-duration rehabilitation need can be served without forcing the user to own an asset that may soon become idle. Ownership, cleaning, maintenance and reuse obligations remain with the specialized supply/rental system. The generic assistive-device rental route is already being organized and is not whitespace.

evidence: A Jiangsu technology-transfer case used a first-use-then-pay arrangement: a university team let an SME test a technical result before committing to a full transfer payment.
After the technology reached the expected effect, the enterprise paid RMB 700,000 and expanded the subsequent cooperation to RMB 3 million.
The enterprise explicitly described the arrangement as reducing uncertainty around investing in new technology.
Jiangsu's current policy framework continues to support first-use-then-pay and allows guarantee/insurance support for this mode.
findings.interpretation: A transaction that is blocked by ex-ante performance uncertainty can form when payment is deferred until decision-relevant evidence exists and the technology provider/guarantee system temporarily bears more of the uncertainty. Generic technology-transfer services are not a new edge; the mechanism is evidence for risk-allocation fit.

evidence: Nantong's 2026 consumer-protection system reported more than 25,000 participating offline no-reason-return merchants on its return platform.
For hard cases involving refusal or delay, a government advance-payment fund pool provides priority compensation and then traces/recoveries from the responsible party.
findings.interpretation: Consumer willingness to transact can be strengthened when refund/fulfillment downside is buffered by an actor with enforcement and recovery capability. This is another non-agricultural replication of risk allocation, not a consumer-platform opportunity for this project.

evidence: First-use-then-pay requires a credible definition and observation of whether the technology reached the agreed effect before payment is triggered.
Equipment leasing depends on legible asset identity, use, maintenance and return/buyout state.
Assistive-device rental requires product qualification, cleaning/reuse rules, maintenance and after-sales accountability.
Advance refund mechanisms depend on transaction/merchant identity and a recoverable responsibility chain.
findings.interpretation: RISK_ALLOCATION_FIT and VERIFIABILITY_TRANSFORMATION are often a compound gate rather than independent mechanisms. Risk can be sustainably moved only when the state/outcome that triggers responsibility is measurable and trusted.
findings.search_rule: Before proposing a risk-sharing structure, identify the exact downside, the actor best able to control it, the evidence that determines when the downside occurred, and the party legally/economically accountable for settlement.

evidence: Jiangsu's 2026 AI+manufacturing plan explicitly uses risk compensation/financial support and asks insurers to explore targeted support around AI+manufacturing pilot/intermediate-test services.
Jiangsu's 2026 scene-opening policy encourages scene-innovation insurance and financial products that provide application-risk protection.

National/ provincial technology-insurance policy supports R&D-loss, technology-transfer-loss and first-set/first-batch insurance and explicitly contemplates insurance around first-use-then-pay technology transfer.
findings.interpretation: Institutions recognize that adoption risk can block new-technology flow, but policy recognition does not prove a current paid missing edge in Xuzhou. Do not promote an AI outcome-insurance or digital-transformation guarantee thesis without a named enterprise case where an otherwise-acceptable project is blocked specifically by outcome risk after existing pilots/subsidies/providers are considered.

search_rules_refined.name: RISK_ALLOCATION_FIT
questions: Which exact downside prevents the exchange from happening?
Which actor currently bears that downside?
Can that actor materially control or diversify the risk?
Is there another actor that can control, pool, price, maintain, insure, recover or reuse the risk-bearing resource more efficiently?
When the risk is reassigned, does a real exchange or usage flow appear?
search_rules_refined.relationship_to_existing_doctrine: Deepening of RISK_BEARING_ORCHESTRATOR and ACCESS_THRESHOLD_COLLAPSE; not a new top-level ontology.

search_rules_refined.name: USE_VALUE_WITHOUT_FULL_OWNERSHIP_RISK
search_rules_refined.pattern: high fixed-cost/reusable asset + intermittent or temporary need + ownership/maintenance/residual risk exceeds user's controllable benefit -> specialist owner retains asset/risk while user buys bounded use
search_rules_refined.boundary: Do not infer whitespace from the existence of rental. Search only for a specific residual where temporary use is desired but current rental/shared-capability routes still impose oversized minimums, unavailable location, rights, maintenance or qualification constraints.

search_rules_refined.name: PAYMENT_AFTER_DECISION_RELEVANT_EVIDENCE
search_rules_refined.pattern: valuable but uncertain technology/service + high upfront commitment risk + measurable result -> trial/use precedes full payment or payment scales with observed result
search_rules_refined.boundary: Outcome-based contracting requires credible measurement and enforceable settlement. Do not call vague satisfaction-based promises a natural connection.

search_rules_refined.name: RISK_REALLOCATION_REQUIRES_VERIFIABILITY
search_rules_refined.pattern: risk transfer without trusted state/outcome evidence creates moral hazard and dispute; durable reallocation requires legible trigger, responsibility and settlement evidence
